statement: Find p_c(G) for a wide class of graphs G. Kesten notes at once that a solution 'would not have any explanatory value': the critical probabilities determined so far depend heavily on special symmetry properties of the underlying graph, and their values vary from graph to graph.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for exact critical probabilities for classes of transitive graphs, plus the arXiv listings of Duminil-Copin and collaborators mined for this intake. Nothing found that computes p_c for a class wider than the self-dual planar lattices and the tree/nonamenable examples already known in 2002; recent activity (Duminil-Copin and Panis 2024-2025, and the high-dimensional survey fetched here as highdim_random_walk_2026) is about exponents, not exact p_c. Kept open. Not exhaustively searched: the isoradial-graph literature, where Grimmett and Manolescu give p_c for a wide isoradial family; that family is a genuine partial answer and is the closest known relative.
title: Exact critical probabilities for a wide class of graphs

statement: For site percolation on Z^d with p > p_c it is known that there are constants 0 < C_4(p), C_5(p) < infinity with C_4(p) <= -n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| = n} <= C_5(p) for all large n. Does lim_{n to infinity} n^{-(d-1)/d} log P_p{|C(v)| = n} exist?
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the surface-order large deviations for supercritical percolation cluster size. Returned the Wulff-construction literature: Alexander-Chayes-Chayes (d = 2), Cerf, 'Large deviations for three dimensional supercritical percolation' (Asterisque 267, 2000), Cerf-Pisztora (2000, 2001), Bodineau (1999). These give a surface-order large deviation principle for the SHAPE of a large finite cluster with speed n^{(d-1)/d} and the Wulff functional as rate. I did not verify from the papers themselves whether they yield the limit for the LOCAL event {|C(v)| = n} rather than {|C(v)| >= n}, at every p > p_c and every d >= 3; the d >= 3 results were originally stated above the slab threshold. Kept admitted with that lead recorded: anyone merging this row should check Cerf-Pisztora before treating it as open.
title: Existence of the surface-order limit for the supercritical cluster-size distribution

statement: For a transitive graph G, is p -> theta_v(p) = P_p(|C(v)| = infinity) left continuous on [p_c, p_u]? Kesten notes that on Z^d, where p_c = p_u, this is equivalent to theta(p_c) = 0, known in 2002 for d = 2 and for d >= 19.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on continuity of theta at criticality for transitive graphs and on the non-uniqueness interval. Fitzner-van der Hofstad (2017) lowered the high-dimensional threshold from d >= 19 to d >= 11, and Hutchcroft has proved theta(p_c) = 0 for large classes of nonamenable transitive graphs and of transitive graphs of exponential growth. I did not find, and did not establish the absence of, a statement covering left continuity on the whole non-uniqueness interval [p_c, p_u] for a general transitive graph. Kept admitted; the Hutchcroft nonamenable results are the closest known relative.
title: Left continuity of the percolation function between p_c and p_u

statement: Prove that the percolation critical exponents (beta, gamma, nu, delta, eta, defined through theta(p), chi(p), the correlation length and P_{p_c}{|C| >= n}) exist as genuine power laws; prove universality, that they depend only on the dimension and not on the lattice; and prove the scaling relations among them. Known in 2002 for site percolation on the triangular lattice and for d >= 19 by the lace expansion, with no progress in d = 3, 4, 5.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for percolation critical exponents in intermediate dimensions 2024-2025. The recent results are on two-point functions: Duminil-Copin and Panis 2024/2025 for the Ising and phi^4 models (sharp for d >= 5, almost sharp with a logarithmic correction at d = 4), and a 2025 revisit of one-arm exponents in high dimensions, plus a spread-out d > 6 derivation of mean-field behaviour. None establishes existence of exponents in d = 3, 4, 5, and none establishes universality in any dimension. Kept open.
title: Power laws, universality and scaling relations for percolation

statement: For Bernoulli percolation on Z^d with 3 <= d <= 5, find upper and lower power bounds for theta(p), chi(p), xi(p) and P_{p_c}{|C| >= n}. Kesten notes that bounds on one side are known for most of these but that no bound of the form theta(p) <= C |p - p_c|^{C'} has been proved for 3 <= d <= 5, not even for p < p_c, and calls this 'probably the most fundamental bound to prove'.
status_search: Same search as E0004. The 2024-2025 Duminil-Copin and Panis lower bounds on two-point functions concern the Ising and phi^4 models and are sharp only for d >= 5 (almost sharp at d = 4); their percolation results are for spread-out models above six dimensions. No polynomial bound of the missing type for nearest-neighbour percolation in d = 3, 4, 5 was found. Kept open.
title: Any power bound at all for percolation quantities in dimensions three, four and five

statement: Let N(v) := inf{number of closed vertices in any path from 0 to v} in critical percolation. On Z^2 it is known that [sigma_{p_c}(N(v))]^{-1}[N(v) - E_{p_c} N(v)] satisfies a central limit theorem, with E_{p_c} N(v) of order log|v| and standard deviation of order (log|v|)^{1/2}. On Z^d with d >= 3 it is only known that N(v) = O(|v|^{eps}) a.s. for every eps > 0. Improve the bound for N(v) and find a limit theorem for N(v) in dimension >= 3.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for the minimal number of closed edges on a path in critical percolation in higher dimensions. The two-dimensional central limit theorem (Kesten-Zhang) remains the standing reference; no d >= 3 result of either kind surfaced. Not exhaustively searched: the high-dimensional chemical-distance literature (Kozma-Nachmias and successors) concerns the OPEN chemical distance, a different functional from N(v), so it does not bear on this row. Kept open.
title: The closed-path functional N(v) in critical percolation in three and more dimensions

statement: In the two-species competition model (a multitype contact process with birth rates beta_i and death rates delta_i), show that species 1 outcompetes species 2 when the two dispersal distributions are the same and beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2. Durrett notes that this is what the Competitive Exclusion Principle predicts and that simulation supports it.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on competitive exclusion for the multitype contact process. Neuhauser's 1992 ergodic theorems for the multitype contact process remain the standing result and cover equal death rates; Cox-Durrett-Perkins (Asterisque 340, 2011) and Durrett's 'Spatial evolutionary games with small selection coefficients' (EJP 2014) cover perturbations of the VOTER model, i.e. a small-selection regime, which is a different hypothesis from the source's beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2 with no smallness assumption. No paper found that proves the stated exclusion for unequal death rates. Kept open.
title: Competitive exclusion in the two-type contact process with unequal death rates

statement: Durrett's Theorem 5 gives coexistence in a stochastic spatial model with fast stirring at rate eps^{-2} whenever there is a function phi that (i) decreases along solutions of the mean-field ODE, (ii) is convex, and (iii) tends to infinity as min_i u_i tends to 0. Formulate and prove a similar general result for systems with LONG-RANGE interactions, where at present the coexistence proofs are done case by case.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for a general long-range analogue of the fast-stirring coexistence theorem. Found the case-by-case long-range results the source cites (Durrett-Neuhauser 1997, Durrett-Lanchier 2008) and the later voter-perturbation programme of Cox-Durrett-Perkins, which is a different limit (weak selection around the voter model, not long range with a fixed nonlinearity). No general long-range theorem with a Lyapunov hypothesis of the source's form was found. Kept open.
title: A general coexistence theorem for long-range interactions to replace fast stirring

statement: In the three-state host-pathogen model of Durrett and Lanchier, show that coexistence is not possible when lambda_2 < lambda_3 < lambda_1. Durrett explains that in this regime the pathogen is a mutualist (it decreases the rate at which the species is replaced), that starting from 1s and 2s in equilibrium with a small density of 3s the fraction of 2s shrinks and the 3s gain an even bigger advantage, and that in this case there is no interior fixed point.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for host-pathogen multitype contact process coexistence results after 2009, including the Lanchier-Neuhauser line of work. Found later host-pathogen and multitype papers but none proving the stated non-coexistence for lambda_2 < lambda_3 < lambda_1. Kept open.
title: Absence of coexistence in the host-pathogen model when the pathogen is a mutualist

statement: Consider the sexual reproduction model with lambda > 4.5. Show that when the stirring rate eps^{-2} is large there is a unique nontrivial stationary distribution. Durrett notes that existence results for stationary distributions are common but convergence results such as the grass-bushes-trees theorem are rare, and that one should start with a concrete case.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on complete convergence theorems for non-attractive spatial models with fast stirring, and on the sexual reproduction (Durrett-Neuhauser) model. Found the existence results and the fast-stirring critical value lambda_c -> 4.5 (Durrett-Neuhauser 1994) but no uniqueness or complete convergence theorem for lambda > 4.5. Kept open.
title: Uniqueness of the nontrivial stationary distribution for the sexual reproduction model with fast stirring

statement: In the catalyst model (states 0 = vacant, 1 = CO, 2 = O; 0 -> 1 at rate p, a pair of neighbouring 0s -> 22 at rate q/4, adjacent 12 -> 00 at rate r/4), find 0 < p_1 < p_2 < 1 so that coexistence occurs for p in (p_1, p_2). Durrett notes that Bramson and Neuhauser proved coexistence when the O_2s are replaced by an N x N polymer with N large, and that Durrett and Swindle proved coexistence in the original model by introducing fast stirring; simulations suggest the O density drops to 0 discontinuously at the upper critical value.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the catalyst / CO oxidation (ZGB-type) lattice model and rigorous coexistence without stirring. The Durrett-Swindle fast-stirring result and the Bramson-Neuhauser large-polymer result remain the rigorous statements; nothing found that removes the small parameter. Kept open.
title: An explicit coexistence window for the catalyst model without stirring

statement: In the colicin model of Durrett and Levin (type 1 produces colicin, which raises the death rate of type 2 by an amount proportional to the local density of 1s), show that coexistence is not possible when lambda_1 < lambda_2 and delta_1 = delta_2 = 1. Durrett notes that in the parameter range where the mean-field ODE has an interior fixed point that fixed point is unstable, and that simulations show segregation with the interface moving in favour of the 1s.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the colicin / allelopathy spatial competition model and rigorous non-coexistence results. Found the Durrett-Levin (1997) analysis and the later interface literature but no proof of non-coexistence under the stated hypotheses. Kept open.
title: Absence of coexistence in the two-type colicin model with equal death rates

statement: Show that coexistence always occurs in the cyclic case of Silvertown's model - the multitype biased voter model on five species with the empirically measured invasion matrix alpha_ij given in the survey, in which i replaces j at rate alpha_ij. Durrett adds: 'For partial credit show that coexistence can occur for some parameters', and remarks that a proof by simulation is given in his Figure 9.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on cyclic multitype biased voter models and rigorous coexistence for more than three species. The three-species rock-paper-scissors and cyclic particle system results (Durrett-Griffeath and successors) are the standing rigorous statements; no five-species result with a general invasion matrix was found. Kept open.
title: Coexistence in the cyclic case of Silvertown's five-species competition model

statement: Show that coexistence can occur in the three-species colicin model, whose mean-field ODE and simulation are given in the survey's Figures 10 and 11.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on three-strain colicin / rock-paper-scissors bacterial competition and rigorous coexistence. The rigorous literature covers the three-species cyclic particle systems and the Kerr-Riley-Feldman-Bohannan style models at the simulation level; no proof for the survey's three-species colicin model was found. Kept open.
title: Coexistence in the three-species colicin model

statement: Show that coexistence can occur in the spatial Prisoner's Dilemma, i.e. in the Hawks-Doves spatial birth-and-death system with game matrix a = -0.6, b = 0.9, c = -0.9, d = 0.7, whose homogeneously-mixing ODE has the Hawk-to-Dove ratio increasing until the population crashes to 0. Durrett reports that simulations suggest Hawks and Doves coexist in the spatial model, because the ODE dynamics happen locally and Doves left behind recolonise space after a local Hawk crash.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on rigorous coexistence in spatial evolutionary games. Cox-Durrett-Perkins, 'Voter model perturbations and reaction diffusion equations' (Asterisque 340, 2011) and Durrett, 'Spatial evolutionary games with small selection coefficients' (EJP 2014, arXiv:1406.5876) determine phase diagrams for spatial games INCLUDING Prisoner's Dilemma cases, but under the hypothesis that the selection coefficient is small (the dynamics is a perturbation of the voter model). Comparing the objects by name: the source's Problem 9 names the Hawks-Doves birth-and-death system with the fixed matrix (-0.6, 0.9, -0.9, 0.7) and no smallness hypothesis, whereas the 2011/2014 theorems name voter-model perturbations with a small selection parameter. Different hypotheses, so the row is kept ADMITTED, with the small-selection results recorded as the closest known relative and the obvious first thing to try.
title: Coexistence in the spatial Prisoner's Dilemma

statement: For the piecewise-deterministic Markov process X modelling the TCP window size (linear growth at unit rate, multiplicative jumps by a factor 1/2 at a state-dependent rate), the generator L has an explicit polynomial eigenbasis and the invariant law's moments satisfy m_n(t)' = n m_{n-1}(t) + (2^{-n} - 1) m_n(t); the polynomials are dense in L^2(mu) but the eigenvectors of L are not orthogonal there (for instance the integral of P_1 P_2 against mu is -64/27). Despite the lack of reversibility, is it possible to use the spectral properties of L to get estimates on the long-time behaviour of X?

The hypocoercivity line (Villani; Dolbeault-Mouhot-Schmeiser) and the Wasserstein/coupling results for this process are what the literature offers; no spectral proof of the ergodicity rate for this specific non-self-adjoint generator was found. Kept open.
title: A spectral proof of ergodicity for the non-reversible TCP window-size process

statement: For the switched linear system dX/dt = A_{I_t} X with I_t a two-state Markov jump process of rate r and A_0, A_1 two fixed 2x2 matrices, let G(r) be the associated top Lyapunov-type functional. Prove Conjecture 4.3: there exists r_c approximately 4.6 such that G'(r) > 0 for r < r_c and G'(r) < 0 for r > r_c, with G(r_c) approximately 0.2, and G(r) -> 0 both as r -> 0 and as r -> infinity. This would imply that the instability set U_alpha = {r > 0 : G(r) > alpha} is empty for alpha > G(r_c) and a nonempty interval for alpha < G(r_c).
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on Lyapunov exponents of two-dimensional Markov-switched linear systems and the shape of the instability domain in the jump rate. Found the general theory (Bene-Chevallier and successors on PDMP Lyapunov exponents) but no proof of unimodality in r for this example. Kept open.

statement: Let X be an R^n-valued Levy process. If for every nonempty proper subspace A of R^n the projection process X_A of X on A satisfies Hunt's hypothesis (H) (every semipolar set is polar), does X itself satisfy (H)?

Equivalently (Question 4): if S is a nonempty proper subspace of R^n and the projections X_S and X_{S-perp} are independent and both satisfy (H), does X satisfy (H)?

The survey records in Section 2 that it is still unknown whether any pure jump subordinator of type-(alpha, beta) satisfies (H), where a pure jump subordinator is of type-(alpha, beta) with 0 < alpha < beta < 1 if its Levy measure has a density nu with c^{-1} x^{-(1+alpha)} <= nu(x) <= c x^{-(1+beta)} for x in (0,1].

The survey's own Theorem 2.29 gives (H) for a subclass of type-(alpha,beta) subordinators under an extra condition; no later paper covering all pure jump subordinators with infinite Levy measure was found. Kept open.

resolved_by: Answered NEGATIVELY inside the source itself. The survey's Section 3.2.1 is headed 'Counterexample for Question 3' and opens: 'We use a counterexample to show that the answer to Question 3 is negative.' The counterexample (PDF p. 16) takes Q = [[2,2],[2,2]], so that sqrt(Q) = [[1,1],[1,1]] and sqrt(Q) R^2 = {(x,y) : x = y}, and a = (1,-1)^T, and sets X_t = a t + sqrt(Q) B_t. Each coordinate-axis projection has a nondegenerate Gaussian part and so satisfies (H) by the survey's Theorem 2.5; the projection on {(x,y) : y = -x} is a uniform motion, which does not satisfy (H); hence X does not satisfy (H) by the survey's Lemma 3.1. Recorded here as an exclusion so that the check is on the record: the objects match by name (the question and the counterexample both concern the coordinate-axis projections of an R^n-valued Levy process), and no external citation is involved.
statement: If the one-dimensional projection process of an R^n-valued Levy process X on each coordinate axis satisfies Hunt's hypothesis (H), does X satisfy (H)?
status_search: No external search needed: the source resolves its own Question 3 two paragraphs after posing it. Recorded as an exclusion rather than silently dropped, so that a merger can see the check.

resolved_by: Zehua Lai and Lek-Heng Lim, 'Recht-Re Noncommutative Arithmetic-Geometric Mean Conjecture is False', arXiv:2006.01510, ICML 2020. Comparing the objects BY NAME: the source calls conjecture (a) the Recht-Re inequality, citing [RR12] = Recht and Re, 'Toward a noncommutative arithmetic-geometric mean inequality', and states it for d x d positive semidefinite matrices with the spectral norm; Lai and Lim's abstract says 'A groundbreaking result of Recht and Re reduces the problem to a noncommutative analogue of the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality where n positive numbers are replaced by n positive definite matrices... The conjectured Recht-Re inequality has so far only been established for n = 2 and a special case of n = 3. We will show that the Recht-Re conjecture is false for general n... which we show are false as soon as n = 5.' Same named conjecture, same objects (n positive semidefinite matrices, sampling with versus without replacement), and the source's own n = 3 status matches the paper's. Correctly excluded. Note: Lai and Lim disprove the inequality without exhibiting explicit matrices, via a noncommutative Positivstellensatz reduction to a semidefinite program, so the counterexample is a certificate rather than a construction.

resolved_by: Rafal Latala, Ramon van Handel and Pierre Youssef, 'The dimension-free structure of nonhomogeneous random matrices', Inventiones mathematicae 214 (2018); arXiv:1711.00807. Comparing the objects BY NAME: the source's question names 'X a symmetric random matrix with independent gaussian entries' and asks whether E||X|| is comparable to E max_k ||X e_k||_2. The paper's abstract, read in full via the arXiv API, opens 'Let X be a symmetric random matrix with independent but non-identically distributed centered Gaussian entries. We show that E||X||_{S_p} is comparable (with universal constants) to E[(sum_i (sum_j X_ij^2)^{p/2})^{1/p}] for any 2 <= p <= infinity', and adds 'This settles, in the case p = infinity, a conjecture of the first author'. At p = infinity the left side is E||X|| (the spectral norm is the S_infinity norm) and the right side is E[max_i (sum_j X_ij^2)^{1/2}] = E max_i ||X e_i||_2 for symmetric X. Same hypothesis, same two quantities, universal constants - this is exactly the source's question. Correctly excluded.

resolved_by: Siddhartha Gadgil and Manjunath Krishnapur, 'Random words in free groups, non-crossing matchings and RNA secondary structures', arXiv:2007.12109 [math.GR] (v1 23 Jul 2020, v3 19 Jan 2022); Indian J. Pure Appl. Math. 54(1) (2023) 146-158, doi 10.1007/s13226-022-00240-x. Quotations below spell Greek letters in ASCII. Comparing the objects BY NAME: the source (arXiv:1406.0763v2, Problem 4, PDF p. 25) asks 'Let (G, mu) be a symmetric measured group and suppose there exists a bi-invariant (conjugation-invariant) and mu-integrable (semi-)metric d on G. Is l_d(mu) = 0?' On its p. 1, G is countable, mu is a probability measure whose support generates G as a semigroup, symmetric means mu(g) = mu(g^-1), and l_d(mu) = lim_n (1/n) int d(g,e) dmu^{*n}(g). The paper (v3, p. 2) sets up: 'fix k >= 2 and consider a random string X = X(n) of length n in 2k letters', 'Let L_k(n) = E l(X(n)) where the expectation is over uniform distribution on strings of length n. Let rho_k(n) = L_k(n)/n denote the average proportion of unpaired letters.' Its Theorem 1 (v3, p. 3) reads: 'With the above notations, rho_k(n) -> lambda_k for some constant 0 < lambda_k < 1.' Its l is the maximal conjugacy-invariant length function on the free group F_k = <alpha_1, ..., alpha_k> with l(alpha_i) <= 1; by its Propositions 7 and 11 the same function is l_CW, the word length with respect to all conjugates of the generators alpha_i, and also the least number of unmatched letters over non-crossing matchings of letters with their inverses. Take G = F_k with k >= 2, mu uniform on the 2k letters alpha_i^{+-1} (symmetric, and its support generates F_k as a semigroup), and d(g,h) = l_CW(g^-1 h). Then d is a metric, left-invariant by construction and right-invariant because l_CW is conjugation-invariant, so bi-invariant, and int d(g,e) dmu(g) = 1. The element represented by the uniform string X(n) has law mu^{*n}, so rho_k(n) = (1/n) int d(g,e) dmu^{*n}(g), and Theorem 1 gives l_d(mu) = lambda_k > 0. Problem 4 therefore has the answer no. The paper also gives 0.034 < lambda_2 < 0.231 and lambda_k -> 1 as k -> infinity (Proposition 15). It does not cite the source, and it does not treat the source's suggested first test case, the stable commutator length on the commutator subgroup of F_2, which is a different function. Earlier work on the same quantity: A. A. Vladimirov, 'Non-crossing matchings', Problems Inform. Transmission 49(1) (2013) 54-57, doi 10.1134/S0032946013010055. Its abstract (OpenAlex record) reads: 'We model the secondary structure of an RNA molecule by means of a maximal non-crossing matching on a random word in a finite alphabet, where ties are only allowed between certain pairs of letters. We prove that the mean fraction of unmatched symbols does not vanish as the length of the word tends to infinity.' Its full text was not read, so which pairings it covers is not checked here, and it is cited as earlier work on the quantity, not as the answer.

result_status: PROVED: yes. For every xi-QSO in which pairs inside a block and pairs containing 0 produce the empty body, y(V(x)) <= (1 - 1/q) y(x)^2 with y = 1 - x_0 (Cauchy-Schwarz on the block masses), so e_0 is the unique fixed point and y(V^n x) <= c^{-1} (c y(x))^{2^n}, c = 1 - 1/q: doubly exponential convergence.
